facts.text: North Vancouver began as Moodyville, a sawmill town founded in 1863 that grew into the largest settlement on Burrard Inlet.
Sewell Prescott Moody bought the failing mill in 1865, renamed it Burrard Inlet Lumber Mills, and turned it into a community with hotel and the inlet's first school.
Arthur Heywood‑Lonsdale financed Moodyville investments in 1882 through Lonsdale Estates, linking the town to a prominent Vancouver land developer.
The Second Narrows Bridge collapsed into Burrard Inlet on June 17, 1958, marking one of British Columbia's worst engineering disasters.
In 2014, North Vancouver officially rebranded its historic waterfront as “The Shipyards,” turning the area into a public gathering spot.
